nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox & compliance review
Oracle legacy DB read-access / migration tooling licenses
Contingency buffer for unestimated backlog items

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based on backlog scope and rate card only.
1 story point ≈ 6 effective hours blended across roles, used to size unestimated tasks by analogy to similarly-described estimated tasks.

Unestimated items (PW-2, PW-4, PW-6, PW-8, PW-10, PW-14, PW-16, PW-18, PW-22, PW-24) were sized by comparison to similar-complexity estimated backlog items; actuals may vary materially once technical spikes are done.

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) carries the largest share of work (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, multi-currency, observability); at 900 hours this is roughly 15 person-weeks per FTE-equivalent over the project, which is a heavy but plausible load for a project of this size — flagged as a risk if timeline is compressed.

Frontend Developer is a single FTE (1.0) covering all UI work including component library, dashboard, accessibility and responsive layout; this role is the likely schedule bottleneck given only 1.0 FTE against ~9 UI-heavy backlog items.

QA Engineer is only 0.6 FTE; testing effort has been scoped conservatively and concentrated on Urgent/High priority items (auth, payments, RBAC, GDPR) — QA coverage on Low priority items will be lighter than ideal.
DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE; hours are concentrated on CI/CD setup, observability and legacy decommission, with limited ongoing capacity for ad hoc infrastructure work.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumes read-only access to the Oracle schema is available early; no budget included for Oracle licensing itself, only tooling.
Non-labour costs are first-year estimates for third-party services/tools and a contingency buffer; recurring SaaS costs beyond year one are out of scope.
Scenario spread (Low/Expected/High) reflects estimation uncertainty on unestimated backlog items and integration risk (Stripe, legacy migration), not schedule risk.
input.reasoning: Labour was allocated by mapping backlog priority and complexity to role effort: Backend Developer takes the majority of hours due to auth, RBAC, payments, migration, multi-currency and observability backend work; Frontend Developer covers all UI-facing tasks including the component library, dashboards, accessibility and responsive layout; QA Engineer effort is concentrated on higher-priority, higher-risk items given limited 0.6 FTE capacity; DevOps Engineer effort covers CI/CD setup, observability tooling and legacy decommissioning within a 0.4 FTE budget. Unestimated backlog items were sized by analogy to comparable estimated items of similar description and priority. Non-labour costs cover third-party tooling/audits directly tied to specific backlog items (Stripe, migration tooling, accessibility audit, observability SaaS) plus a general contingency for the unestimated items given the uncertainty. Three scenarios (Low/Expected/High) reflect the estimation risk from unestimated points and integration complexity (payments, legacy migration), with Expected as the primary planning number equal to the sum of all line items.

reductions.description: Descope PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API) — both Low priority and not required for core portal launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~70 Backend and ~30 QA hours; defer to a post-launch phase.

reductions.description: Defer PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff) to a later phase; support staff can use direct DB/read-only tooling in the interim.
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated 100 Frontend and 30 Backend hours from this phase.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of PW-14 (Multi-currency support) to display-only (no settlement) for launch, adding settlement later.
reductions.effect: Cuts an estimated 50 Backend hours of settlement/FX-reconciliation logic.

reductions.description: Defer third-party accessibility audit (non-labour) until after internal accessibility pass (PW-15) is validated, re-testing only if issues remain.
reductions.effect: Removes the external audit line item; relies on internal QA/dev accessibility testing initially.

reductions.description: Reduce contingency buffer from $8,000 to $4,000 once PW-2, PW-4, PW-8, PW-10, PW-16, PW-22 and PW-24 are formally pointed by the team.
reductions.effect: Lowers non-labour contingency; only safe once unestimated items are actually sized.
